outcome: Other adverse maternal and perinatal health outcomes
cohort: Mothers who gave birth in Ontario, Canada between 2002 and 2014, including 34,233 refugee immigrants, 243,439 non-refugee immigrants, and 615,394 Canadian-born mothers.
finding: While refugees and non-refugee immigrants experienced similar odds for most adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes compared to Canadian-born mothers, refugee mothers had a significantly higher odds of HIV compared to non-refugee immigrant mothers from the same country of birth.
mod_finding: Refugee mothers had slightly elevated odds of cesarean section compared to non-refugee immigrants (AOR 1.04, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.08).
